architecture_decisions.recommendation: Removed react-dom from required peer dependencies in both @trpc/react-query and @trpc/tanstack-react-query packages
architecture_decisions.rationale: React DOM is only required for web environments, not for React Native/Expo. Making it a required peer dependency forces React Native developers to install an unnecessary package that they don't use, which can cause installation conflicts and bloats their projects. By removing it from required peer dependencies, we maintain compatibility for web developers (who will still install react-dom anyway) while allowing React Native developers to use tRPC without unnecessary dependencies.
alternatives_considered: Marking react-dom as optional peer dependency (peerDependenciesMeta)
Creating separate packages for web vs React Native
Using conditional imports with try-catch blocks

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Kept react as a required peer dependency while making react-dom optional
architecture_decisions.rationale: React itself is required for all React environments (web, React Native, Expo), while react-dom is specific to web environments. This distinction allows the package to work across the entire React ecosystem without forcing unnecessary dependencies on non-web platforms. The change maintains backward compatibility because web developers will continue to install react-dom as part of their normal setup.
alternatives_considered: Removing react dependency entirely (not feasible as tRPC React hooks need React)
Using peer dependency optional flags instead of removal

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Applied the same change to both @trpc/react-query and @trpc/tanstack-react-query packages
architecture_decisions.rationale: Both packages provide similar functionality with different React Query versions, and both are used by React developers across different environments. Consistency ensures that developers using either package get the same React Native compatibility benefits. This also simplifies maintenance and documentation since the dependency requirements are identical across both packages.
alternatives_considered: Using workspace dependencies to manage this centrally

tickets.title: Make react-dom optional for React Native compatibility
tickets.description: Update peer dependencies in tRPC React packages to allow React Native and Expo usage without requiring react-dom

implementation_summary:
The change implements React Native compatibility by removing react-dom from the required peer dependencies in both @trpc/react-query and @trpc/tanstack-react-query packages. This is a minimal, surgical change that addresses the core issue: React Native and Expo developers don't use react-dom, but were forced to install it due to tRPC's peer dependency requirements.

The approach maintains react as a required peer dependency since all React environments need it, while recognizing that react-dom is web-specific. This change is backward compatible because web developers using React DOM will continue to install react-dom as part of their normal development workflow. The package will still function correctly in web environments since react-dom will be present, while React Native environments can now install tRPC without unnecessary dependencies.

By applying the same change to both packages, we ensure consistency across the tRPC React ecosystem. This pattern follows the principle of minimal dependencies and respects the different requirements of web vs native React environments. The implementation requires no code changes because tRPC's React integration doesn't actually require react-dom at runtime for its core functionality—it only needs React itself for hooks and component lifecycle management.
